messages:
cheng: pushed the cross-region kernel comparison charts to the doc, looks noisy. wondering when we should flip defaults from Triton->Flashv3 for H100 in us-west vs europe-west.
maya: saw that — flashv3 wins p50 on long seqs but p99 gets weird on asia-east for small batch sizes. did you include the kv-cache hit rate?
sam: yes, kv-cache varied by region due to our request pattern. us-west had ~35% prefix reuse, asia-east ~8%.
cheng: here's the short bench snippet I ran:
```bash
./bench --model redwood-7b --kernel flashv3 --gpu h100 --region us-west1 --seq 4096 --batch 1
# result: p50 62ms, p99 420ms, tok/s 220
./bench --model redwood-7b --kernel triton --gpu h100 --region us-west1 --seq 4096 --batch 1
# result: p50 80ms, p99 380ms, tok/s 190
```
liza: interesting — flashv3 improves median but p99 is higher in that run. could be scheduling tails. did you try batching=4?
cheng: batching=4 on flashv3: p50 55ms, p99 260ms, throughput up 2.8x.
maya: for A100 we saw Triton + cuBLASLt still competitive, especially for q8 quantized models. flashv3 q8 on a100 had a small quality regression in our eval set.
sam: +1 on eval regression. We should gate default kernel switch on (1) no eval perf regressions, (2) regional tail SLOs met, (3) cost per token improvement >10%.
benchmark-bot: :white_check_mark: nightly-kernel-compare finished for redwood-7b across 3 regions. Artifact: https://artifacts.internal/bench/1793456789
liza: ops ask: what about capacity sizing impact? if flashv3 reduces avg GPU utilization but increases p99 we might need more headroom for SLA.
cheng: yep. I computed rough capacity delta: flashv3 in us-west reduces tokens/GPU by ~12% at p50 but needs +8% headroom to keep p99 under 500ms. net cost ~neutral unless heavy prefix reuse.
maya: rule of thumb: switch when prefix reuse >=20% or 95th token cost drops >15% on short seq. else keep Triton for stability.
sam: can we add a canary policy: route 10% traffic for new kernel per region, monitor p99, quality evals, cost delta for 24h before promoting?
liza: yep that's standard. also add automatic fallback to Triton on p99 > 600ms for any route.
cheng: I'll draft a runbook and a small checklist (eval pass, canary thresholds, capacity calc) and drop it in the onboarding doc.
maya: thanks — will add region-specific notes (asia needs extra caution). :thumbsup:
sam: ping me when ready, I'll schedule a dedicated slot to run larger A100 comparatives.
benchmark-bot: :information_source: archived raw logs at s3://redwood-bench/1793456789.tar.gz
